chapter: Louis Armstrong, Gene Krupa and the drum school
title: Gene Krupa

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Let's talk about Gene a bit.
Oh Gene. Well the thing that I always say

about Gene is, See, any time, I've been knowing Gene way when he was with Mal Hallett's band, I was with Blanche Calloway. I met Gene in Boston, Mass, the New England states. Gene, and I think it was Chubby Jackson, Carmen Cavalerra was with Mal Hallett's band, and that was 1933, that's how long I been knowing Gene, up through the years when he first joined Benny and just everything, Gene knew me when I was with Benny Carter, and Willie Bryant and all up through those years. But, when the fact still remains, when you really find out a person is when you're up there dealing with him with that money. See, and Gene and I, we going in a few thousand apiece on that school. Well any time that you can exchange those thousands together and never squawk, you all right. Well that's the way it was with Gene Krupa. Never a word said about nothing. Just go on and do it and that was it, and we exchanged thousands of dollars together. Never nothing bad said, no arguments, why did you do this, why did you do that? Nothing like that. So, that's what I've always said about him.
Just about everything you hear about him is like that.

Yeah, yeah, great, great person. I knew his wife, Ethel. I knew them, see I knew Gene way before they got married to Ethel. They were all with Benny Goodman; I knew Allen Reuss's wife before they married; they were all with Benny. How Gene met his wife, she was a telephone

operator at the Higby Hotel, I think that was the name of it, right across from the Paramount Theatre. And she used to call Gene in the morning to wake him up for the first show, that's how they met. Allen Reuss, knew his wife before they married. Artie Bernstein, knew his wife before they were married.
Well did you see much of Gene, say in his last years?

Yeah, yeah we just did one of his last concerts when we dedicated at Shea Stadium, out there at Louis Armstrong, Gene was on that. That's the last time I saw him alive, and he had invited Evelyn and I to his home, but before we got there, he'd passed. And I'm the first one he called when Ethel dropped dead.
Oh really? When did that happen?
That was when he was in the Bronx, in I think--
He had a house in Yonkers that burned down right? About a year before he died.

Some rustic place, Rustic Drive. Yeah, Yonkers, burned up all his music and everything. Yeah, Gene and I were real tight. Very dear friends. Gene Krupa. Very nice cat, very nice person. He's responsible for bringing drums up front.
I think we talked about yesterday, you were probably the first drummer besides him who was featured
with a big band, weren't you?
Yeah, I would say that, yeah. Of course, Chick Webb, he featured himself.
But he wasn't featured that much in solos, was he?
No.
He was a great ensemble player.
Yeah, yeah.
But they didn't build drum features around him.
Around him, no. It was Gene and then me, and then I think Buddy.
